title: edaphos: Digital Soil Mapping with Causal, Physics-Informed and Generative Methods
description:
edaphos is a research-oriented R package for digital soil mapping beyond regression-tree models, organised around ten methodological pillars:

  1. Causal inference — backdoor adjustment on pedogenetic directed acyclic graphs, instrumental variables with first-stage and Sargan diagnostics, Cinelli–Hazlett sensitivity analysis, and LLM-assisted causal-claim extraction.
  2. Physics-informed depth modelling — a closed-form pedogenetic ODE and Neural ODEs.
  3. 4D pedometry — stacked ConvLSTM forecasting and Ensemble Kalman Filter assimilation.
  4. Foundation models — SimCLR / MoCo-v2 contrastive pre-training on raster patches.
  5. Active learning — with physics-informed rejection gates.
  6. Quantum machine learning — a ZZFeatureMap kernel simulator and quantum kernel ridge regression.
  7. Bayesian hierarchical spatial models — Gibbs, RcppArmadillo and spBayes backends.
  8. Neural operators — DeepONet and the Fourier Neural Operator.
  9. Diffusion models — denoising diffusion for soil-map patches.
  10. Graph attention networks — over k-nearest-neighbour co-location graphs of profiles.

A common edaphos_posterior class lets seven of the ten pillars be scored with the same calibration diagnostics (CRPS, PICP, MPIW). The deep-learning pillars use torch when libtorch is available and a pure-R reference path otherwise.

Real-data benchmarks on WoSIS profiles from the Brazilian Cerrado are reproducible from the scripts in data-raw/; the package ships aggregate results, not third-party soil measurements. The reported results include negative ones: foundation-embedding instruments are strong but fail the Sargan over-identification test, and on the real-data benchmark several frontier pillars do not outperform a DAG-informed linear model.

Version 2.0.0 is the first release since 1.6.0. The development history between them used internal labels (1.7.0–4.1.0) that were never released or deposited.
